cases.question: In first-game packet setup, which sites/pawns/garrisons/denizens/advisers are faceup or facedown, and where is Ivory Eye?
cases.reason: The named placements, garrisons, advisers, and Ivory Eye are correct. However, this question explicitly asks faceup/facedown states. The expected answer and required facts F01–F03 omit faceup for the starting denizens (and leave the three starting sites implicit through “Other sites facedown”). The printed setup spread resolves those states directly. Adding faceup is a precision repair to an existing asked clause, not a new question or a newly discovered rule.

every_asked_clause.assessment: Placements and counts correct; explicit starting card orientation needs precision.
every_asked_clause.source_result: Plains is faceup at top Cradle with the purple pawn, two purple warbands, and faceup Longbows; Mountain is faceup at top Provinces with red/blue pawns, one purple warband, and faceup Taming Charm; Rocky Coast is faceup at top Hinterland with yellow pawn, one purple warband, and faceup Elders. Five other sites are facedown. Pawn and warband pieces have placement/count, not a faceup/facedown card state.

cases.implicit_versus_missing: The phrase “Other sites facedown” reasonably implies that the three named starting sites are faceup, so this is not an incorrect placement ruling. Law 5.1.4.I also makes ordinary play to a site faceup. That action rule supports the intended setup state, but it does not expressly state the initial packet setup operation. More decisively, merely naming Longbows/Taming Charm/Elders at their sites does not explicitly answer their orientation. The original setup diagram, rather than a new inferred rule, supplies the requested faceup state. The adviser state is already explicit in the existing answer and mapped clause, so no separate F04 correction is required.

cases.question: Can a player rule a facedown site or put cards there using a move power? What does a ruined edifice contribute to capacity, suit and action access?

every_asked_clause.source_result: Only faceup sites can be ruled, by player or bandits. Facedown sites cannot hold cards, including cards moved there by a power. A move power cannot bypass the errata prohibition.
locators: Errata, Rules Errata and Additions, Law 2.8 Site Cards: “Facedown sites cannot hold cards.”
Errata, Glossary Rule: adds face-up to player and bandit site rule.
Law p.11 Glossary, Move: location changes follow restrictions; Rule.

every_asked_clause.assessment: Capacity, suit, major-action use, and power access are all covered.
every_asked_clause.source_result: A ruin is the ruined side of an edifice card. Each edifice card counts toward the site’s combined denizen/edifice card capacity; the ruined side has no suit and cannot be used to Muster or Trade. It still has its printed power. Ordinary card-power access is available if the player rules the card (including rule through its site) or their pawn is at the site with it, subject to power text/type exceptions.
locators: Law p.4 2.8.1 Card Capacity and 2.9 Edifice Cards.
Law p.9 Powers introductory text, 7.1.1 Access, 7.1.4 Persistent Powers, 7.3.2 Action, and 7.5.1 Added Use Limit.
Law p.11 Glossary Rule: site ruler rules cards at that site.

cases.implicit_versus_missing: No separate sentence saying “a ruin is an edifice card for capacity” is needed: 2.9 defines ruined and intact as sides of the same edifice card, and 2.8.1 counts edifice cards. The existing F02 states that result directly. Likewise, “power still functions per access/text” in the existing answer and F03 invokes the general power rules. Operationally that means rule the ruin (usually by ruling its site) or have your pawn at its site, subject to exceptions such as persistent powers ignoring access and battle plans requiring rule. The key need not repeat the whole power-access chapter to remain correct. It must not be interpreted as forbidding every action power just because Muster/Trade cannot use the ruin as their chosen card.
cases.confidence: high; direct definitions, actions, power rules and explicit official errata agree
